prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The 2019 Conservative manifesto promises to get Brexit done immediately with Boris Johnson’s “oven‑ready” deal, taking the whole UK out of the EU, single market and customs union, ending ECJ jurisdiction, and striking global free trade deals without political alignment to the EU. A Conservative majority is framed as the only way to end paralysis, avoid two more divisive referendums under Labour/SNP, and unleash Britain’s potential through a strong, pro-business, low-tax, One Nation agenda.

Core guarantees and priorities
- NHS and social care: Record funding, 50,000 more nurses, 6,000 more GPs, 50 million extra GP appointments, 40 new hospitals/20 upgrades, an Innovative Medicines Fund, mental health treated with the same urgency, free parking for those in greatest need, a fast‑track NHS Visa, and no NHS in trade talks. Social care: £1bn extra each year, cross‑party reform with a guarantee no one has to sell their home to pay for care, more support for carers, and doubled dementia research.
- Law and order: 20,000 extra police, fair and proportionate stop and search, tougher sentences (ending automatic halfway release for serious crimes; whole-life terms for child murder), new knife crime orders, more prison places, a national cyber force, stronger NCA, a Victims’ Law and Domestic Abuse Bill.
- Controlled immigration: An Australian-style points system prioritising skills and contribution; fewer low‑skilled migrants; equal treatment for EU and non‑EU citizens; NHS surcharge and benefits only after five years; Windrush justice; fast‑track routes for NHS staff and top global talent; stronger integration and English language support.
- Opportunity and levelling up: Extra £14bn for schools, teacher starting salaries at £30k, firm discipline and Ofsted, arts and sport investment, and a £3bn National Skills Fund, upgraded colleges, Institutes of Technology, more apprenticeships on major projects.
- Economy and tax: Keep the rates of income tax, VAT and NI frozen; raise the NI threshold; maintain the pension triple lock; improve Universal Credit; back small business with a business rates overhaul, late‑payment crackdown, start‑up loans, higher Employment Allowance; boost R&D (towards 2.4% of GDP), strengthen anti‑avoidance and implement a Digital Services Tax—while keeping Britain the best place to start and grow a business.
- Infrastructure and housing: A transport revolution (Northern Powerhouse Rail, Midlands Rail Hub, roads, restored Beeching lines, better buses and cycling), rapid EV charging, gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025, a Towns Fund and cultural investment, and a million more homes with “infrastructure first,” local design standards, building safety reform, green, beautiful homes, protected Green Belt, long‑term fixed‑rate mortgages, local discounts, fairer shared ownership, a Better Deal for Renters (ending ‘no‑fault’ evictions).
- Environment, rural and coastal: Net Zero by 2050; 40GW offshore wind by 2030; carbon capture, hydrogen and nuclear; £9.2bn for energy efficiency; clean air laws; plastics crackdowns; powerful environmental watchdog; tree and peatland restoration; support for farmers (public money for public goods) and fisheries (independent coastal state), and animal welfare reforms.
- Union, democracy and global Britain: Strengthen the UK’s Union, Shared Prosperity Fund, freeports, oppose a second Scottish referendum; voter ID, defend free speech and a free press; constitutional review to restore trust; 2%+ defence with Trident, Space Command, support for veterans; a Magnitsky sanctions regime; 0.7% aid for girls’ education, media freedom and modern slavery.

The choice: a decisive Conservative majority to deliver Brexit, stability and a high‑skill, high‑wage, low‑tax future—or Labour/SNP chaos, more referendums, higher taxes and uncertainty.
